issues.legal_issue: A lease agreement is concluded when the agreed land schedule is delivered for annexation in accordance with the agreement.
material_facts: The lease agreement referred to a schedule of the lands to be annexed.
The defendant testified that an extract identifying the disputed land was delivered to the senior family member for annexation after the agreement was executed.
The trial court, the district court, and the Judicial Commissioner accepted that evidence.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent finding that the parties had a concluded lease agreement was accepted.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted the lower courts’ factual finding that the land extract was delivered pursuant to the agreement’s terms, completing the agreement despite the schedule not being incorporated in the copy produced in evidence. No earlier case was cited on this issue.

rule.if: supreme_court_appeal and lease_required_land_schedule and land_extract_delivered_for_annexation and lower_courts_accepted_delivery

predicates.supreme_court_appeal: The matter is before the Supreme Court in an appeal challenging a finding about whether a lease agreement was concluded.
predicates.lease_required_land_schedule: The agreement contemplated that an identified schedule of land would be annexed to it.
predicates.land_extract_delivered_for_annexation: A party delivered an extract identifying the land to the other contracting side for annexation in accordance with the agreement.
predicates.lower_courts_accepted_delivery: The lower courts accepted the evidence that the land extract was delivered for annexation.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges lease formation, the agreement required an identified land schedule, the extract was delivered for annexation, and the lower courts accepted that delivery, the agreement is treated as concluded.

issues.legal_issue: An unregistered instrument affecting immovable property may be used to show the character of a person’s possession, but not to establish a property right that the instrument required registration to create.
material_facts: The defendant relied on a copy of an unregistered agreement that purported to grant a fifteen-year lease of land.
The defendant relied on the agreement in support of his claim that his possession was as a tenant.
The agreement could not create the claimed fifteen-year tenancy because it was unregistered.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was inadmissible to prove the right to a fifteen-year tenancy, but its recitals could be relied on to show the character of the defendant’s possession.
issues.legal_principle: Section 49 of the Indian Registration Act, 1908, read with the registration requirements in Section 17 and the Transfer of Property Act, bars an unregistered document from proving a transaction affecting immovable property that required registration. The proviso to Section 49 permits its use for a collateral purpose, including showing the character of possession. The Court relied on Padma Vithoba Chakkavva v. Mohd. Multani and referred to Varatha Pillai v. Jeevanatkammal.

predicates.civil_property_possession_dispute: The proceeding concerns a dispute about possession of immovable property.
predicates.unregistered_property_instrument: A party relies on an instrument affecting immovable property that was not registered although registration was required for it to create the claimed right.
predicates.instrument_used_to_show_possession_chara: The instrument is relied on to show the character of possession rather than to establish the property right that required registration.

issues.definition: In a property-possession dispute, an unregistered instrument that is relied on to show the character of possession is admissible for that collateral purpose, though it cannot establish the unregistered property right.

issues.legal_issue: A fact-dependent challenge to a person’s authority to grant a lease cannot be raised for the first time in the Supreme Court when it was not argued below and requires factual investigation.
material_facts: The plaintiffs challenged the lessor’s authority to grant the lease for the first time in the Supreme Court.
The challenge had not been argued before either the district court or the Judicial Commissioner.
Resolving the challenge would require investigation of facts.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to consider the challenge to the lessor’s authority.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Court’s settled practice, a question not raised before the High Court is not considered for the first time in the Supreme Court when its resolution requires investigation of facts.

predicates.supreme_court_appeal: The matter is before the Supreme Court in an appeal.
predicates.issue_not_raised_below: The party did not raise the issue before the lower appellate courts.
predicates.issue_requires_factual_investigation: Resolving the issue would require investigation of facts.

issues.definition: In an appeal before the Supreme Court, an issue not raised below and requiring factual investigation is not considered for the first time.
